subject: Food Science
title: European Horse Meat Scandal
description: A micro-lesson that makes European Horse Meat Scandal usable.

hook.text: In 2013, DNA testing revealed that 'beef' burgers in British and Irish supermarkets contained up to 29% horse meat.

buildup.text: The scandal started when Irish food inspectors routinely tested frozen beef burgers.

discovery.text: Investigation traced the contamination through a labyrinth of middlemen across six countries.

twist.text: Horse meat isn't dangerous—it's eaten legally in France, Italy, and Japan. The scandal was about fraud and traceability failure.

climax.text: The EU mandated DNA testing for meat products and strengthened traceability requirements.

punchline.text: European Horse Meat Scandal: the goal is not certainty, but sharper thinking.

quiz.question: What was the core issue in the European horse meat scandal?
options: Fraud and traceability failure—horse meat was safe but intentionally mislabeled as beef
